mcqs.question: Who announced that the 8th Economic Census would be conducted in 2027?
mcqs.explanation: Statistics Secretary Saurabh Garg announced the 8th Economic Census for 2027. The Registrar General & Census Commissioner is associated with the Population Census, while Lord Mayo and W.C. Plowden are linked with earlier census milestones.

mcqs.question: Which sequence correctly describes the planned Population Census and 8th Economic Census?
options: Population Census in 2026–27 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027
8th Economic Census in 2026 followed by Population Census in 2027
Population Census in 2027 followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2026–27
Both censuses will be conducted simultaneously in 2026–27
mcqs.explanation: The two-phase Population Census is scheduled for 2026–27, followed by the 8th Economic Census in 2027. The other options reverse or incorrectly merge the sequence.

mcqs.keyword: Census authority, law and constitutional provisions
mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in the context of Indian census and backward-class provisions.

List-I
(a) Registrar General & Census Commissioner
(b) Census Act, 1948
(c) Union List, Entry 69 and Article 246
(d) Article 340

List-II
(i) Authority under the Ministry of Home Affairs
(ii) Legal basis under which individual census data is confidential
(iii) Constitutional placement of the census subject
(iv) Commission on backward classes
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. The Registrar General & Census Commissioner functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs; the Census Act, 1948 protects individual data confidentiality; Entry 69 places census in the Union List; and Article 340 concerns a commission on backward classes.

mcqs.question:
Match the census year with its milestone.

List-I
(a) 1830
(b) 1872
(c) 1881
(d) 1921

List-II
(i) First synchronous census
(ii) Great Divide
(iii) First complete census of a city
(iv) First all-India non-synchronous census
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are 1830–first complete census of a city, 1872–first all-India non-synchronous census, 1881–first synchronous census and 1921–Great Divide. The Great Divide reflected the only decadal decline, of -0.31%, associated with the 1918 flu.

mcqs.question:
Match the census year with the associated milestone.

List-I
(a) 1971
(b) 1991
(c) 2001
(d) 2011

List-II
(i) Fertility decline in EAG States
(ii) ICR technology used
(iii) Question on fertility of currently married women
(iv) Literacy counted for the 7+ age group
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are 1971–fertility of currently married women, 1991–literacy for the 7+ age group, 2001–ICR technology and 2011–fertility decline in EAG States. Each alternative misplaces at least two of these milestones.

mcqs.question: Which combination contains the ancient sources that contain references relevant to population enumeration?
options: SBI Act, Banking Regulation Act and RBI Act
Imperial Bank, State Bank of India and Banks Board Bureau
mcqs.explanation: The Rigveda, Arthashastra and Ain-i-Akbari, written by Abul Fazl, contain the cited ancient references. The other combinations contain modern laws, constitutional provisions or banking institutions.

mcqs.keyword: SECC, Article 340 and State survey powers
mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?

1. The SECC 2011 was the first caste enumeration since 1931.
2. Article 340 provides for a commission on backward classes.
3. State powers for such surveys are located in the Union List, Entry 20.
4. SECC 2011 data was confidential and could not be used for scheme targeting.
mcqs.explanation: Exactly two statements are correct: statements 1 and 2. State survey powers are associated with Concurrent List Entries 20, 23 and 30, not the Union List; SECC 2011 data was not confidential and was used for scheme targeting.

mcqs.keyword: Caste survey and Criminal Tribes Act
mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Patna High Court struck down the Bihar caste survey, and the Supreme Court issued no notice.
Statement B: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 was a colonial law that labelled tribes as “born criminals”.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false: the Patna High Court upheld the Bihar caste survey, while the Supreme Court issued notice. Statement B is true because the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 used the label “born criminals” for tribes.

mcqs.question: Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, what is the maximum number of nominees permitted per account?
mcqs.explanation: The amendment permits up to four nominees per account. Nomination may be simultaneous, with percentages totalling 100%, or successive in the case of lockers; the other options misstate the permitted number.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The threshold for “substantial interest” was raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹1 crore.
Statement B: The maximum tenure of cooperative bank directors was increased from 8 to 10 years, excluding the chairperson and whole-time directors.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false: the threshold was raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore. Statement B is true; the maximum tenure became 10 years, excluding the chairperson and whole-time directors.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding cooperative-bank directors under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 is incorrect?
options: The chairperson is excluded from this tenure limit.
The reform aligns with the 97th Amendment.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the maximum tenure remains 8 years. The correct maximum is 10 years, excluding the chairperson and whole-time directors, and the reform aligns with the 97th Amendment.

mcqs.question: What replaced the requirement to report on the “last Friday” under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025?
options: The first day of the month
The last day of the month or fortnight
The first Friday of the month
The last working day of the year
mcqs.explanation: The phrase “last Friday” was replaced by “last day of the month/fortnight.” The other dates do not represent the amended reporting timeline.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The maximum tenure of cooperative bank directors under the reform is 10 years.
Reason (R): The maximum tenure under the reform is 15 years.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true because the prescribed maximum tenure is 10 years. Reason R is false: the tenure is not 15 years.

mcqs.question: The State Bank of India Act, 1955 transformed which institution into the State Bank of India?
mcqs.explanation: The SBI Act, 1955 transformed the Imperial Bank into the State Bank of India. The Banks Board Bureau and Urban Cooperative Banks are separate banking entities or structures, while the Reserve Bank of India was not transformed into SBI.

mcqs.question: How many banks were nationalised in 1969, before further nationalisation in 1980?
mcqs.explanation: Fourteen banks were nationalised in 1969, followed by further nationalisation in 1980. The other figures do not match the 1969 nationalisation exercise.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020 brought cooperative banks under RBI control.
2. The RBI Governor is the chairman of the Banks Board Bureau.
3. Urban Cooperative Banks were brought under the Banking Regulation Act by the 1966 amendment.
mcqs.explanation: Exactly two statements are correct: statements 1 and 3. The 2020 amendment brought cooperative banks under RBI control, and Urban Cooperative Banks were brought under the Banking Regulation Act by the 1966 amendment; the RBI Governor is not the chairman of the Banks Board Bureau.
